faqs.a: You must be aged 16 to 32 when you start initial training as a Royal Marine Commando. Commonwealth applicants applying from inside their country of origin must be at least 18, while those already resident in the United Kingdom may apply at 16. If you are under 18, a parent or guardian must consent to your joining.
faqs.q: What age can I join the Royal Marines?

faqs.a: No, there is no minimum qualification requirement for the Royal Marine Commando role, although a good standard of general education is important. Musicians and buglers are the exception: they must read music and play an instrument to a high standard. Fitness, medical suitability, nationality and security clearance matter far more than exam results for commando applicants.
faqs.q: Do I need qualifications to join as a commando?

faqs.a: Applicants face a pre-joining fitness test, a fitness assessment and the Royal Marine Candidate Preparation Course, followed by a four-day selection phase. Tests cover running endurance, press-ups, sit-ups, pull-ups and swimming, with standards that rise through training. Consistent running, strength work and pool practice before applying give candidates the best chance of success.
faqs.q: What fitness tests must Royal Marines applicants pass?

faqs.a: Starting salary during training is £26,334 per year, with pay rising as marines progress through the ranks. Additional allowances may apply for some jobs and overseas service, and the package includes subsidised food and accommodation, uniforms, free healthcare and a pension. Senior ranks can earn substantially more over a full career.

headline: Join the Royal Marines in 2026
metaDescription: Royal Marines recruitment in 2026: age, nationality, fitness and medical rules for commandos, plus training, pay and the step-by-step application process.

sections.content:
Royal Marines Commando applicants must be aged 16 to 32 when they start initial training, and there is no minimum qualification requirement for the commando role. Applicants must be nationals of the United Kingdom, Commonwealth citizens or dual nationals, and Commonwealth applicants applying from their home country must be at least 18.

Under-18s need consent from a parent or guardian. Every applicant must also pass a medical examination, a security check and a swimming assessment, and must declare tattoos and previous convictions during the process.
sections.title: Who can apply

sections.content:
Fitness is the defining test for Royal Marines selection. The official standards set a maximum BMI of 28, with possible exceptions when waist measurement is under 94 cm, and a minimum weight of 65 kg or a minimum BMI of 23. Applicants must also meet the minimum height of 145 cm.

The pre-joining fitness test and the candidate preparation course assess running, strength and endurance, followed by a four-day selection phase. Swimming ability matters too: candidates must pass the naval swimming test, including pool work and water confidence exercises.
sections.title: Fitness standards

sections.content:
Successful candidates begin the 32-week commando course at the Commando Training Centre Royal Marines in Lympstone, Devon. The course builds fitness, fieldcraft, weapons handling, navigation and amphibious skills, and it ends with the commando tests that earn the green beret.

Training is deliberately demanding and attrition is high, so preparation matters more than raw talent alone. Applicants are advised to build running endurance, upper-body strength and swimming confidence well before the selection weekend, and to practise the tests under fatigue.
sections.title: Training at Lympstone

sections.content:
Starting pay during training is £26,334 per year, rising with rank and experience, with potential earnings reaching around £64,790 for senior ranks according to career guidance. Marines also receive subsidised food and accommodation, free healthcare, a pension and seven weeks of paid leave plus public holidays.

After training, marines specialise in areas such as assault engineering, combat intelligence, heavy weapons or mountain leadership. Careers can lead to officer selection, specialist qualifications recognised in civilian life, and service around the world at short notice.
